content: I will update [next.config.ts](file:///c:/Users/jorda/OneDrive/Documents/SITE%20SEU%20MARQUINHO/next.config.ts) to permit loading images from `lh3.googleusercontent.com`. This will allow us to use the gorgeous lifestyle background images from the mockup, while still keeping the local product photos.
thinking:
**Refining The Layout**

I've successfully configured the custom CSS. My next step involves updating `src/app/page.tsx` to align with this new layout and style. I'm focusing on the header, starting with the title/logo text and its styling, which I'm considering as `<span className="font-sans font-black tracking-tighter text-xl uppercase text-[#E0E0E0]">`.


**Adjusting Text and Styles**

I've revised the header text with `font-display font-extrabold text-2xl md:text-4xl tracking-tighter text-primary dark:text-primary-fixed`. I am using Tailwind v4 custom colors, with `primary` as `#fff9f3` and `primary-fixed` as `#ffe179`. The active link now employs `border-primary-container`, and other links use `text-on-surface-variant dark:text-on-surface-variant hover:text-primary transition-colors`. Finally, the cart badge will have a red background, using `bg-[#d30017] text-[#ffe2de]`.


**Configuring Image Sources**

I'm now focused on image handling, specifically the hero background. The user provided an external URL for a high-contrast cinematic image. I realized that using the `<Image />` component in Next.js with an external URL necessitates configuring `next.config.ts`. I'm verifying if `lh3.googleusercontent.com` is permitted, understanding the potential for build failures if it's not. It seems best to allow this domain in `next.config.ts`, ensuring compatibility with external and local images. I'm taking a closer look at all the image URLs provided in the HTML.


**Prioritizing Asset Integration**

I'm now prioritizing the integration of local image assets. The user has a `public/PRODUTOS E LOGO/` folder with brand images, and I must use the specified filenames for the `src` attributes of the Next.js `<Image />` components. The updated plan focuses on using these local files while retaining the black background, Montserrat font, gold accents, and exact layout.
